title: Books the Bible Quotes
lead: The Bible sometimes quotes or names writings that are not in it: lost Israelite books, Greek poets, and Jewish works like 1 Enoch. How should we understand these quotations? This page is about books the Bible quotes or names; for which books are in the Bible, see the canon page.

sections.b: The Old Testament cites several books we no longer have: the Book of the Wars of the LORD (Numbers 21:14), the Book of Jashar (Joshua 10:13; 2 Samuel 1:18), and the records of prophets such as Nathan and Gad (1 Chronicles 29:29). The writers used them as sources, much as a historian today cites older records.

Paul quotes Greek poets: "In him we live and move and have our being" and "we are his offspring" (Acts 17:28), "Bad company ruins good habits" (1 Corinthians 15:33), and a Cretan prophet (Titus 1:12). He also names Jannes and Jambres, Pharaoh's magicians, known only from Jewish tradition (2 Timothy 3:8). Quoting a true saying does not make its whole source Scripture.
